If Taira struggles to get the grappling going Van is going to brutalize him with his elite boxing. Give me Josh van +$$$$.

My gut tells me Waldo, my brain tells me Volkov. Without research I am leaning Volkov.

Sean Brady is in a weird place. He was riding high but his wins are ageing like dried up cow ****. He was TKO'd by pillow hand Belal and Michael Morales made him look like an amateur. Buckley struggled with Usman's wrestling (who very much still has plenty in the tank) so if Brady gets his wrestling going Buckley could lose a decision. With that being said Buckley has a lot of power and if Brady can't survive a pillow barrage from Belawl muhammed I don't think he will be able to survive some Buckley hammers. Buckley By KO/TKO.

Jeremy Stephens is 1-8 in his last 9..... His win was against a cardboard box with a current 11-10 record. Bobby green walks around with his hands down and pieces him up to a Unanimous Decision.

R.i.P Ozzy Diaz lmao. Gautier is going to hurt him.

Yaroslav vs Joel Alvarez is such a banger of a fight. Yaroslav has too small of a UFC sample size for me to have an early read on this. This deserves to be on the main card. Why are we clowning around with Bobby Green and Jeremy Stephens? I get that will probably be a fun fight, but this will too and this fight actually means something.

Grant Dawson is basically the mirror spiderman version of Sabatini, elite wrestler with chin issues. I don't remember how Rebecki's takedown defense is and that is entirely what this fight is going to come down to unless he pulls off a flash knockout. More research is needed here, but Rebecki is solid as hell despite being 1-3 in his last 4. Leaning Dawson right now. Rebecki only has 1 KO in 7 UFC fights and i think that is his only path to victory.

Jared Gordon isn't a sexy name but he certainly isn't bad. Jim Miller is 43..... gimme flash.

I am a Kopylov hater and for good reason, he is middy mid mid. Tulio let me down in his last fight and I am not sure if he is any good.  He is the last one to beat Yousri who is good. Kopylov's best best win is Puna Soriano if you're into that sort of thing. (I'm not). Without doing further research I am using MMA math and going Tulio.

Sabatini is very very good. His fatal flaw is his chin, William Gomis is conservative and has zero power so I don't see his chin being an issue. Sabatini by sub or dominant decision.

Djorden Santos is tough as hell so I don't think Susurkaev gets a finish, but he keeps his 0.

The Clayton Carpenter hype train has fully derailed. Despite Ochoa being 1-2 in the UFC he has looked very good and has lost to Top tier opponents.

posts.content:
Prediction:
Chimaev  |  Submission  |  Round 2

Volkov vs. Cortes-Acosta
Alexander Volkov, DEC
This is a really tough one to call since it's hard to gauge what level either of their skillsets are at. I guess I'll go with Volkov since he beat up Pavlovich pretty good when Waldo lost to Pavlovich. The fight with Waldo was pretty close though as Waldo won R1 and R2 was firmly Pavlovich but it wasn't like he ran away with the fight. Waldo's record is a tad inflated as he beat Lewis who is kind of a free win these days based on his mood, Delija who is 1-2 in the UFC, and Gaziev who is a blob. At least Volkov had a close striking match with Gane who's arguably the best in the division. He did have to grapple and who knows, maybe he will try a takedown on Waldo here. Waldo has really grown on me and regardless if he wins or not, I hope he gets a shot at the title someday. The one thing that makes me hesitate on being more confident in Volkov, is that it seems like Waldo has been getting more confident the longer he fights in MMA. He went from boxing where he got KOed 3 times (surprisingly his chin is pretty good in MMA), to fighting 5 fights in regionals, to the UFC. He was a decision machine until recently and it really seems like he's found his groove and feels confident with the flow of MMA. I have to respect the fact that he had 0 takedowns attempted in the UFC and knew the danger Robelis was so he grappled him all fight even though that wasn't his strong suit. 95% of fighters would not do that. Look at all the guys fighting Pereira who aren't attempting any takedowns, too much ego. I'm not sure what to call that, but that's the mentality of a champion. Volkov's reach, experience, and overall skill might be a bit too much for him here, but I hope Waldo wins and I'll be rooting for him

posts.content:
Prediction:
Chimaev  |  Submission  |  Round 1

Volkov vs. Cortes-Acosta
Alexander Volkov, DEC
This fight should take place on the feet and Volkov is the more technical striker of the two and has a wider variety of weapons he can go to. I also believe he'll be the one walking forward and throwing more volume in this fight. Waldo is more of a counter puncher and his biggest weapon is that overhand right. If Volkov can stay disciplined with his distance management, work the jab, work the leg kicks/body kicks, and just avoid the counter right from Waldo, he should cruise to a clear UD. Waldo's only win condition here in my opinion is to catch Volkov and put him out. Volkov has been knocked out in the past, but he's been much more locked in later on in his career, so I trust him to stay safe and pull this one out.

posts.author: DevinM34
posts.content:
Prediction:
Chimaev  |  Submission  |  Round 1

Brady vs. Buckley
Sean Brady, SUB, R3
This fight with Buckley is much different than Brady's fight with Morales. Morales controlled the center of the octagon and kept his hips far back where Brady couldn't even begin to shoot a takedown on him. Buckley is lighter on his feet and sometimes will skate around the outside. Usman and Colby were both able to take him down when he got pushed back behind the black line near the cage. The difference in those two fights was Usman was able to control him and keep him from using the cage to get back to his feet whereas Colby obviously could not. Brady has excellent control and I think the takedown opportunities will be there. Buckley does have power and Brady is hittable so maybe he bonks him, but I feel pretty good Brady can get his game going and either win a clear DEC or find a SUB. The only X factor here is Buckley has been training with Usman, so maybe he's improved his takedown defense and is smarter about being on the backfoot. I have to go with what I see on tape though.

Rarely does that happen, and more often than not fans get robbed of matchups like this. Round 1 will be classic Borz, however Strickland stays composed. The next 2 rounds you start to see the same sort of style and engagement but with Strickland having much more success staying upright. Rounds 4 and 5 Chimaev becomes much more willing to pace himself and strike which allows Strickland to really force his fight here. Strickland has incredible success keeping distance and jabbing and staying out of diving ankle pick range. It starts to look vibrantly scary here for Chimaev. They start throwing actual haymakers at each other and both fighters land. Chimaev takes one last attempt for a takedown to dodge brutal incoming strikes. He secures a takedown. Some will think that's enough, other's will think Strickland is/was deserving of a victory here. As someone who had Strickland over Izzy Twice, This fight does not seem so obvious as it does on the surface. I have leaned Chimaev every fight since he has entered the UFC...I think Strickland's go-out-on-his-shield energy might be one of the more underrated MMA superpowers. Wow. I officially pick Sean Strickland to upset Khamzat Chimaev 48-47x2, 46-49 Split Dec

Van vs. Taira
Joshua Van, TKO, R2
Taira will be too willing to strike for my liking here, Just the act alone will allow Van to get on the inside of the longer-reached Taira. Van will see this strategy and get to the destination faster than Taira. Great fight for a while but Van forces an exchange that puts Taira down on the mat. Van does not let up here and the Ref jumps in after several moments of brutal ground and pound. TKO Victory for Van. AND STILL!

29-28x3 Volkov survives a scare to secure a decision victory overcoming WCA's pace and lack of engagement with brutal jabs and leg kicks.

posts.content:
Prediction:
Chimaev  |  Submission  |  Round 3

Clayton Carpenter vs. Jose Ochoa
Jose Ochoa via Decision
They must like having Clay open up numbered events. With Clay he can start off fights strong but gets figured out quickly if he can’t control the action. Ochoa also has his warts but he’s got more ability to hurt and stagger Clay which will give him the edge in this one. If Clay is able to get this to the mat and make it dicey for Ochoa then things might get interesting but I’ll go with the Peruvian to get his hand raised.

Baisangur Susurkaev vs. Djorden Santos
Baisangur Susurkaev via 1st Round TKO
Building up Susurkaev by giving him a proper can to crush. I’ll be a bit disappointed if he lets this one drag out longer than it should.

Pat Sabatini vs. William Gomis
William Gomis via Decision
I have a funny feeling about this fight. Classic striker vs grappler matchup but are we sleeping on Gomis here? I know is style can be a bit stale but it’s effective and Pat can struggle against good strikers. It all comes down to can Gomis keep Pat at bay and not let him get his gameplan implemented, and I think the younger Gomis can keep him off him and get this one done.

Roman Kopylov vs. Marco Tulio
Roman Kopylov via 1st Round TKO
Dogs gotta bark in this card folks. I’m not high on either of these two but Tulio still leaves too much to be desired while Kopylov has had a couple really tough matchups recently. They both can hurt each other but I think Kopylov has more determination and skill to put Tulio down in the 1st with a big time knockout.

Jim Miller vs. Jared Gordon
Jared Gordon via Decision
🎶Just what, just Unc it up. What, just Unc it up. Just please? Just Unc it up. Unc, Unc Unc it up🎶 this is a throwback in the literal sense. Might be it for Jimbo but the future Hall of Famer has an untouchable legacy that’ll forever be remembered and especially for his Lauzon fight. As for Jared, he might not have much left in the tank but it’s always nice to notch a win against a name that’s big to add to your resume.

Grant Dawson vs. Mateusz Rebecki
Grant Dawson via Decision
I love Rebecki’s style because he’s 100% entertainment value but it comes at a price of losing your long term durability. Grant could finish him but he just got finished himself recently and usually fighters get a bit cautious when it comes to taking risks that might not be worth it next time out. Could expect a lot of control time implemented by Grant to stymie Rebecki but that won’t stop Rebecki from still trying to press and take command. Ultimately Dawson will prove to be too much and take the Decision victory.

Joel Alvarez vs. Yaroslav Amosov
Joel Alvarez via 3rd Round TKO
Dogs keep howling here folks. Also, why in the bloody **** is this not higher than Gautier vs Diaz on this card? What are we doing? Anywell, this is an absolute banger of a fight and should deliver. I’m still wondering where Amosov will ultimately settle in the UFC pecking order and this might be where we find out. Alvarez is tough wherever the fight goes and is starting to his prime just in time to make some noise at Welterweight. Amosov won’t be able to dictate any grappling like he’d prefer and that might make him a bit demoralized as the fight goes. If he starts to fade in the 3rd, Alvarez will start to turn up the action and get the late stoppage finish.

Ateba Gautier vs. Ozzy Diaz
Ateba Gautier via 1st Round TKO
A can will be crushed, next fight please.

Bobby Green vs. Jeremy Stephens
Bobby Green via 1st Round KO
Let’s double up on some Unction in Newark. Bobby will get another finish over a Jeremy Stephens that’s also likely done after this fight. You’re a legend Jeremy, it’s time.

Sean Brady vs. Joaquin Buckley
Sean Brady via 2nd Round Submission
Fun contrast in styles in a big time fight at Welterweight. Brady wants to maintain his contender status while Buckley is still looking to prove himself worthy of being one. Brady will have a substantial edge in grappling and now it’s just a question if he can get it to the mat, which he should be able to. Buckley is going to have to put Brady down and he most definitely has the power to do so but Brady will be smart on the feet. He’ll get Buckley to the ground in the 2nd and lock in a Kimura to hand Buckley his first submission loss of his career.

Alexander Volkov vs. Waldo Cortes-Acosta
Alexander Volkov via Decision
Waldo’s run to a title shot hits a Russian road block here. Volkov will have the length and grapple advantages while Waldo has sound technique on the feet. Volkov has a bit more experience with these kinds of matchups and that’ll show as the fight goes on. If Waldo was a more dynamic finisher I’d maybe sway his way but he’s just not. Volkov will show his experience and fortitude to take a Decision victory.

Joshua Van vs. Tatsuro Taira
Tatsuro Taira via 2nd Round Submission
Japan, you have yourself a UFC champion. When you see the size difference between these two and realize how much of an edge Taira has in grappling, you’re hoping Van has the power to knock him out. He does, but Taira is an uber smart fighter who knows not to welcome a fire fight and especially in a title fight. He’ll take a round to download the data as they say, then start to find ways to attack Van in the 2nd and if he gets his back, this is wraps. Taira locks in a 2nd round RNC and becomes your new UFC Flyweight Champion.

Khamzat Chimaev vs. Sean Strickland
Khamzat Chimaev via 3rd Round Submission
Now we’re on to the fight we’re all waiting to see. Sean just had the best performance of his career and he’s going to need to replicate it to get the strap. Khamzat looked near dead on the scale and usually this is where karma rears its ugly head. But Khamzat’s different, he’s so skilled at what he does and is now motivated to finish Sean. Sean can’t let Chimaev get his hands on him and drain the will out of him. It’s just a formality tho and in the 3rd Khamzat locks in a brutal Face Crank to retain his title….but will move to Light Heavyweight right afterwards. This weight cut is too much for him at this point.

posts.author: ChrisSweeney
posts.content:
Prediction:
Chimaev  |  Submission  |  Round 1

Chimaev vs. Strickland
Khamzat Chimaev, SUB, R1
After watching Khamzat vs. DDP, I said to myself I will never choose against Chimaev for his entire career. Strickland looked good in his last fight, but this matchup is a much tougher challenge. While he has good takedown defense, he hasn’t really faced consistent, high level wrestling pressure like Khamzat Chimaev brings. Chimaev has shown he can wrestle hard for a full 25 minutes and overwhelm opponents quickly. Even when Strickland faced Dricus, he had trouble defending takedown attempts, which raises concerns about how he’ll handle someone like Chimaev. (Pretty sure Abus had his back early too) Although he wasn’t held down for long, the ease of those entries is worrying. He’s also hyping Khamzat up, Strickland has been talking a lot of trash, including personal comments, which might motivate Chimaev even more. And since they’ve reportedly sparred before with Chimaev getting the better of it, that adds to the concern for Strickland. I think Khamzat does Khamzat things and shoots within the first 20 seconds and it goes his way from there.

Van vs. Taira
Tatsuro Taira, SUB, R2
Great fight, Kinda happy it got moved to this stacked card. Taira’s gonna show levels though. Taira’s main strength is his elite grappling. Once he gets positions like the back or top control, he can take over rounds quickly and create submission threats. He’s shown he can dominate opponents on the ground and only needs one successful sequence to completely shift the fight. Even when his wrestling isn’t perfectly clean, his ability to scramble and transition into control positions makes him extremely dangerous. His striking is solid,He has underrated early power. He tends to be more effective when he can mix striking into entries for his grappling rather than extended stand-up exchanges. Van’s biggest improvement has been his takedown defense and ability to get back to his feet, but he still hasn’t faced a grappler at Taira’s level. While he’s shown he can defend shots and survive grappling heavy situations, this is a major step up in both control ability and submission threat. If Taira is able to secure top position, Van will be dealing with one of the most dangerous grapplers in the division as a Blue belt. While Van is a serious and improving opponent, Taira’s grappling is the most fight defining skill in this matchup. If he can consistently get the fight to the mat, he has the clearest path to control, dominance, and potentially a finish through submissions or ground-and-pound.

Volkov vs. Cortes-Acosta
Alexander Volkov, DEC
Another great fight that makes sense, I’ve been a very big fan of Waldo on this run but I know when to call his losses, I picked Pavolich and I expect the same kind of technical performance from Volkov. Most of Waldo’s success has come against opponents who either aren’t very durable or were willing to brawl with him. We’ve seen Waldo’s limitations against elite competition not that long ago. Volkov is elite competition and a much more technical and experienced striker. He uses his size, reach, jab, and kicks very well, and he’s improved his overall game, especially defensively and in grappling. While he has had some controversial or boring fights, he’s still proven to be a high-level heavyweight who can manage distance and control fights from range. Stylistically, Volkov doesn’t need to engage in wild exchanges to win. He can stay at range, use his kicks and jab, and frustrate Waldo, who tends to struggle when he can’t close distance easily. Waldo’s striking has improved and he hits hard, but his boxing can still be a bit sloppy compared to elite heavyweights, and he hasn’t consistently proven he can hurt top tier durable fighters. 3x 29-28 Volkov.

Brady vs. Buckley
Sean Brady, DEC
King of Philly bounce back. I’m pretty split on this matchup though, Buckley has improved a lot at 170 and can definitely win if he keeps it standing, but his grappling weaknesses are still very clear. His takedown defense is decent at range and early in exchanges, but once he’s pressured to the cage or put on his back, he struggles to get back up. That’s a major concern against someone like Brady. Brady’s biggest strength is chaining takedowns and controlling opponents once he gets them to the fence or mat. That lines up well with Buckley’s biggest weakness. Even if Buckley defends a few early shots, Brady’s pressure style likely leads to repeated attempts and long control sequences. Overall, it’s a classic striker vs grappler matchup. Buckley’s path is keeping it standing and capitalizing on power, while Brady’s path is consistent takedowns and control. Given Buckley’s history against strong wrestlers and Brady’s proven ability to grind, Brady slightly feels like the more reliable pick, even if the upside on Buckley’s side is very real. I see the line movement and I don’t care.

Green vs. Stephens
King Green, DEC
Unless Green gets sent into the afterlife by a big meaty hook which is possible, this should be a clear win for Bobby Green. You expect Stephens to try to turn this into a scrap, but I don’t think he’ll be able to consistently land cleanly or deal with Green’s movement and jab. Green is better at range, more efficient with output, and harder to hit cleanly, while Stephens has slowed down and absorbed a lot of damage over his career. There’s even a chance of a late KO if Stephens takes too much damage. I think WhoThe*** is done in the UFC atleast. 3x 30-27 Green.

Gautier vs. Diaz
Ateba Gautier, TKO, R1
Another no-test for Ateba. Ateba’s last performance was a bit disappointing, but it still showed some positives. He proved he can keep power late into fights and survive longer than expected. This is a showcase fight made for Ateba to score another highlight reel knockout and build momentum heading into bigger opportunities later on. Which might take another 3 fights with how the UFC is treating him.

Alvarez vs. Amosov
Joel Alvarez, TKO, R2
Yes i’m biased, This is the only good Spanish fighter until Sosa develops or someone new comes in. So I have to back my countrymen. I am scared for him in this match-up, but he can win this. Joel moving up in weight adds a lot of unknowns. He’s still a big, physical fighter for the division and extremely dangerous on the feet, but there are questions about how his style will hold up against stronger grapplers like Yaroslav. Yaroslav is a proven Bellator fighter and a very good grappler with good pace and control. He may not be an elite finisher on the mat, but he is consistent at getting takedowns and staying on top. His striking is more cautious but he’s generally functional enough to close distance and force grappling exchanges. At 170, the main concern is Joel’s grappling defense against elite wrestlers. While he has good submissions off his back and a dangerous guard, he doesn’t have strong wrestling or reliable takedown defense. He tends to accept bottom position and look for submissions rather than actively controlling scrambles or getting back up. But if the fight stays standing, Joel has a clear advantage. He’s faster, more creative, and hits much harder, especially with his reach and dynamic striking. The key issue is whether Joel can keep the fight upright against a larger and more capable wrestler than he’s used to, that becomes a serious test. His defensive habits and tendency to rely on guard play could give Yaroslav consistent top control if takedowns come through. I’m rocking with my boy still more UFC proven.

Dawson vs. Rębecki
Mateusz Rębecki, TKO, R1
This is one of the toughest fights on the card to predict because both guys have very clear strengths and weaknesses. And the matchup feels extremely dependent on who can force their game first. Dawson is the better pure wrestler and grappler by a wide margin, but recent fights have made it clear that his entire game revolves around getting takedowns. On the feet, he can’t do anything it looks like. Rebecki has flaws too, but stylistically this matchup could work well for him. He’s the much better striker, pressures nonstop, attacks the legs, and forces chaotic exchanges. The big question is whether Rebecki can defend against the wrestling. However, he’s explosive, physically strong, and fast to get up. I think Rebecki hits him clean before Dawson can build up control time.

Miller vs. Gordon
Jared Gordon, DEC
Crafty vet fight. Miller is still dangerous early and remains a crafty veteran, especially with his grappling and power, but at 42 years old he’s clearly slowing down. He can still beat lower-level opponents and older veterans, but whenever he faces solid competition now, the athletic and cardio differences become obvious. He’s slower, more hittable, and tends to fade badly after the first round. Gordon should have the major advantages in speed, volume, cardio, and overall striking. Gordon is much faster and more active. His jab, combinations, and pace should give Miller serious problems, especially once the fight settles in. The fight likely becomes one-sided as Gordon starts overwhelming him with volume. 3x 30-27 Gordon.

Kopylov vs. Tulio
Marco Tulio, DEC
Low confidence, Should be a cool high-level striking fight. Kopylov is a very skilled striker with clean kickboxing, fast kicks, and good precision, but he has shown clear struggles against pressure heavy fighters who force him into uncomfortable exchanges. His recent losses against Robocop and Costa also exposed issues when opponents mix durability with forward pressure and don’t give him time to settle into his rhythm. Tulio is a high output pressure fighter who thrives in chaotic exchanges. Even if his technical skillset isn’t as good as Kopylov’s, his aggression, pace, and willingness to engage can disrupt more technical strikers. He doesn’t need perfect form, he needs constant pressure and volume. There are concerns about Tulio’s defense and chin, but he has shown he can compete through adversity and push a hard pace over multiple rounds. Kopylov has had cardio questions of his own and sometimes fades mentally or physically in longer fights, even if he remains dangerous. The key factor is pace. If Tulio forces this into a high volume boxing match and keeps Kopylov under pressure, he can turn it into a grinding, uncomfortable fight where Kopylov’s technical edge is reduced. Tulio’s forward pressure and durability give him a clear path to make this competitive. 3x 29-28 Tulio.

Sabatini vs. Gomis
Pat Sabatini, SUB, R2
Two niche fighters I really like, but after the Chepe performance and because he’s a Philly fighter I'm gonna rock with Sabatini. Both guys are extremely consistent with their approaches. Gomis is the cleaner striker and much better on the feet, while Sabatini has a massive grappling advantage and probably the clearest path to victory overall. Gomis has solid takedown defense and is difficult to control for long periods, but he hasn’t faced a wrestler or grappler at Sabatini’s level before. In previous fights, strong grapplers have been able to give him problems once they got him down. He can survive and scramble, but his defensive grappling off his back has looked shaky at times. That’s a major concern here because Sabatini is one of the stronger wrestlers and grapplers in the division. He’s very good at chaining takedown attempts together, controlling opponents against the cage, and keeping pressure on once he gets top position. He’s also consistently been able to take opponents down throughout his UFC run. Sabatini will likely have plenty of opportunities to shoot for takedowns without dealing with major danger coming back at him. Once the fight hits the ground, it feels like Sabatini has the ability to dominate and potentially find a submission or ground-and-pound finish.

Susurkaev vs. Santos
Baisangur Susurkaev, TKO, R2
I don’t like Susurkaev, I don’t think he’s that great but Susurkaev is the much more talented fighter here, even if he hasn’t fully lived up to the hype yet. Santos is low level. He’s extremely durable and aggressive, but not particularly skilled. His whole game is based on nonstop pressure, high volume, and toughness. But toughness won’t win a fight if that’s all you have. Susurkaev is the cleaner and more skilled striker by a wide margin. I think he should be able to pick Santos apart at range. Susurkaev has the advantage in the wrestling too, and mixing in takedowns could make the fight much easier for him. I expect Susurkaev to find the finish because he’s the more skilled fighter no matter where the fight goes. If he fights seriously he should find a finish easily.

Carpenter vs. Ochoa
Jose Ochoa, TKO, R2
I think Ochoa is just a level above Carpenter. Carpenter is more well rounded and has a BJJ edge, but he’s not top tier in any one area besides grappling, and he’s gotten outgrappled by better competition. Ochoa is the opposite style wise, a big, aggressive Chute Boxe-type brawler with nonstop pressure, good cardio, and heavy Muay Thai. Weak takedown defense but he’s shown he can get back to his feet and stay dangerous. His biggest weapons are pressure, toughness, and body kicks. He’s only lost to Kavanaugh and Asu, who are both top 10 guys, and he put up great fights for a fighter who’s only 8-2. The key question is whether Carpenter can consistently wrestle and control him. Carpenter has the grappling advantage on paper, but his control isn’t great and he can be reversed or forced into scrambles. Ochoa’s physical strength and ability to get back up could neutralize a lot of that. On the feet, Ochoa has a big advantage. Carpenter is hittable, keeps his chin high, and tends to struggle in longer striking exchanges. I think Ochoa neutralizes the wrestling, finds the chin and proves he’s the better prospect.
